correctness.rationale: For f=sum a_k z^k set P(u)=sum |a_k|^2 alpha^{-k}u^k; then M_2(f,r)^2=P(alpha r^2) and norm^4=2∫P(u)^2e^{-2u}du exactly. The positive-weight factorial moments m_j=j!/2^(j+1) are strictly log-convex under either candidate Q. Consecutive ratios pinpoint one (lower half) or two (upper half) minimizing degrees and yield <P,Q> >= <Q,Q> P(s)/Q(s) for all positive coefficients. Cauchy-Schwarz proves sharpness, and its equality case forces P proportional to Q. Direct algebra evaluates the piecewise constants and coefficient ratios. At s=0, constant functions are uniquely sharp. The standalone standard-library checker passed 560 exact rational inequalities and 153 certificate/boundary/origin identities; finite checks do not prove the global theorem.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating theorem establishes best possible growth order but does not determine the best constant or extremizers. The theorem computes the entire sharp envelope for a natural first non-Hilbert radial exponent and proves a qualitative change in optimizers across every half-integer radius threshold. The exact two-monomial transition gives reproducible sharp examples that are absent from the monomial growth-order tests, and may guide other mixed exponents.
